steps.name: GSVA hallmark pathway scores per sample
caveats: GSVA >= 2.0 uses the param-object API: build GSVA::gsvaParam(expr, geneSets, kcdf='Gaussian', minSize=10) (or ssgseaParam for method='ssgsea') and call gsva(param) — the old positional call signature is deprecated and errors in 2.6
Genes absent from the 12,000-row matrix are simply unmatched; report how many hallmark members were matched per set rather than assuming full coverage

If the staged hallmark GMT cannot be read, fall back to the WikiPathways human GMT (/mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt, same symbol space) and state the substitution
steps.context: Reference: MSigDB human hallmark gene sets v2026.1, HGNC symbols GMT (h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, 50 sets, HALLMARK_* names). The expression input is the VST matrix from T1S1; genes are symbols, matching the GMT directly. The executing agent resolves the staged GMT against /mnt/refs at run time.
steps.question: For each of the 12 samples (6 treated, 6 control): what is its activity score for each of the 50 MSigDB hallmark pathways, computed by GSVA on the VST-normalized expression matrix?
constraints: Use gene symbols as the identifier space end to end (GMT is HGNC symbols, counts rows are symbols)
kcdf='Gaussian' because the input is VST-transformed continuous expression, not ranks of raw counts
Score all 12 samples so every sample gets a value for every pathway
min set size 10, max 500 (all 50 hallmark sets fit this range); do not silently drop sets without listing them
steps.description: Read the staged MSigDB human hallmark GMT (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols), intersect set members with the 12,000 input gene symbols, and compute a per-sample pathway activity score for every sample with the GSVA package (method='gsva', kcdf='Gaussian' on the VST matrix; report set sizes after filtering and drop sets below minSize=10). Output a pathways x samples score matrix (approximately 50 x 12) plus a log of how many hallmark genes were matched per set.
acceptance_criteria: Hallmark GMT parsed; number of sets and per-set matched-gene counts after intersection with the expression matrix reported
Sets falling below the minimum size threshold listed and dropped explicitly
Score matrix written as CSV with one row per hallmark set and one column per sample (samples in metadata order)
Method parameters (method, kcdf, min/max set size) recorded in the output summary

steps.name: Differential hallmark activity test and heatmap
caveats: Scores are correlations/linear-combination statistics, not absolute activities; between-sample comparisons of the same pathway are valid, cross-pathway magnitude comparisons are not
If sample_01 sits apart from its group in the heatmap, note it as a possible library-size remnant rather than a biological effect
steps.context: Input: the ~50 x 12 GSVA hallmark score matrix from T1S2 and the condition labels from metadata. limma and ComplexHeatmap are installed; the heatmap is the direct answer to 'a heatmap of the hallmark activity across the samples'.
steps.question: Which of the 50 hallmark pathways differ in activity between UC treated (6) and control (6) samples, and what does the samples x pathways heatmap show about how the two groups separate?
constraints: BH FDR across the tested hallmark sets; report the number of sets passing FDR < 0.05 and, if none do, report nominal p-value ranking instead and say so
Z-score each pathway row across the 12 samples before heatmap coloring; annotate columns with condition
Do not merge correlated sets or apply additional shrinkage; keep the 50-set hallmark collection intact
steps.description: Fit limma (~condition) on the GSVA score matrix to identify hallmark pathways differentially active in treated vs control (moderated t-test, BH FDR), and render a ComplexHeatmap of z-scored hallmark scores with columns annotated by condition and rows ordered by differential activity, so the separating pathways are visible at a glance.
acceptance_criteria: limma results table written with per-pathway log2 fold change, moderated t, raw and BH-adjusted p-value, sorted by effect size
Heatmap written with 12 condition-annotated sample columns and z-scored hallmark rows; top separating pathways labeled
Group-mean difference per pathway reported with direction (up in treated vs control)
Small-n caveat stated alongside the results: 6 vs 6 unpaired samples limits power and no replication cohort is available here

plan.title: GSVA hallmark pathway scores for UC treated vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw Salmon gene-level counts for 12 colon samples (6 UC treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, 12,000 genes; sample_01 has ~4x lower library size). To answer 'which pathways separate treated from control with a per-sample score', the pipeline is: (1) DESeq2 normalizes the counts (size factors absorb the library-size imbalance of sample_01), filters low-count genes, and produces both a variance-stabilized expression matrix (the per-sample expression input for pathway scoring) and a gene-level differential expression table (context for interpreting pathway shifts); (2) GSVA/ssGSEA converts the normalized per-sample expression matrix into a per-sample pathway activity score matrix against the 50 MSigDB hallmark gene sets, which are staged as an HGNC-symbol GMT matching the gene-symbol rows of counts.csv; (3) limma on the score matrix tests each hallmark for treated-vs-control differential activity with BH FDR, and a ComplexHeatmap of z-scored hallmark scores with condition annotation shows which pathways separate the groups. The directory name and question indicate GSVA-style sample-level scores specifically, so per-sample quantification (not gene-set permutation on a ranked gene list) is the core method; scGate TME models and other staged references are irrelevant here and are not used.
